subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Injunctive Norms: What Others Approve Of
description: A quick, practical guide to Injunctive Norms: What Others Approve Of.

hook.text: A smiley face on your energy bill if you use less than neighbors. A frowny face if you use more. Simple.

buildup.text: Injunctive norms signal what others approve or disapprove of. They add a moral layer on top of descriptive norms.

discovery.text: Schultz found the smiley face prevented the boomerang effect. Low users kept saving because they knew others approved.

twist.text: The approval signal doesn't need to be explicit. A green checkmark, a congratulations banner — all convey social.

climax.text: The strongest nudge combines 'this is what people do' with 'this is what people think is right.' Together they're.

punchline.text: We do what others do. Even more what others praise.

quiz.question: How do injunctive norms differ from descriptive norms?
options: Injunctive norms signal social approval or disapproval
Injunctive norms have no effect on behavior

details.summary: Injunctive norms communicate what others approve or disapprove of rather than what they actually do. While descriptive norms say what most people do, injunctive norms say what most people think you should do. Both influence behavior but through different psychological mechanisms.
details.whyItMatters: Injunctive norms add moral weight to behavioral nudges. When combined with descriptive norms, they prevent the boomerang effect where above-average performers relax their behavior.
takeaways: Injunctive norms convey social approval or disapproval of a behavior
They work through the desire for social acceptance rather than information about what is typical
Combined with descriptive norms, they prevent the boomerang effect

faq.question: How is an injunctive norm different from a descriptive norm?
faq.answer: A descriptive norm says 'Most of your neighbors recycle.' An injunctive norm says 'Your neighbors approve of recycling.' One provides information about typical behavior; the other signals social approval. Both motivate but through different channels.

faq.question: When should injunctive norms be used instead of descriptive norms?
faq.answer: When the descriptive norm is undesirable, such as when most people litter, using descriptive norms would backfire by normalizing the bad behavior. Injunctive norms work by communicating disapproval of the behavior regardless of how common it is.
